Related work The importance of autonomous systems in precision farming has ex- ponentially grown in the last few years (Thayer et al., 2020; Berenstein and Edan, 2018; Williams et al., 2020; Xiong et al., 2020). A modern vision-based yield estimation approach is a complex system capable to detect, track and map the fruits collecting streams of images. Such a system consists of different functional modules, among which the most relevant is certainly the fruit detection module. Its purpose is to detect and locate the fruits within a single image. Solutions that rely on LIDAR or differential GPSs are expensive and place important constraints on the overall system, especially with respect to power and weight requirements and the availability of a network of fixed ground reference stations for the GPS correction. These aspects considerably limit the diffusion of such approaches and may not be accessible to small and medium farms with limited financial resources. The acquisition of these labels is costly, burdensome and time- consuming, which considerably slows the deployment phase of the yield estimation system in new crops or orchards. Furthermore, to obtain reliable annotations, expert human operators that are familiar with vision-based detection and segmentation methods need to be involved. If we also consider that it is very hard to train DNNs that robustly generalize over scenarios not observed during training ( e.g., unseen fruit categories, different cameras, different weather conditions) without further optimization or fine-tuning procedures, it is clear how the practical applicability of vision-based solutions for yield estimation is further limited. Inspired by the previous considerations, we propose a novel yield estimation system that benefits from the advantages of vision sensors and, at the same time, exploits a weakly supervised paradigm to heavily reduce the effort needed to train the DNNs (see Fig. 1). Differently from state-of-the-art methods, our approach is a com- plete system capable to detect, track and build a graphical map with the position of the detected fruits using only a monocular camera and a minimal amount of supervision. As we discuss in the following sections, all the modules in our system are designed to keep to a minimum the annotation efforts, by either exploiting weak supervision that requires simple and easy-to- compute labels or by relying on publicly available pre-trained models that do not need further optimization or fine-tuning ( e.g., depth and optical flow estimation modules). Furthermore, our approach requires only a monocular camera and does not make any assumption on the underlying platform: the sensor can be either mounted on ground or aerial robots, or hand-held by a human operator. Related work The importance of autonomous systems in precision farming has ex- ponentially grown in the last few years (Thayer et al., 2020; Berenstein and Edan, 2018; Williams et al., 2020; Xiong et al., 2020). For the yield estimation task, alongside range sensors ( e.g., LIDAR or lasers), there is increasing adoption of vision-based methods (mostly based on CNNs) that are very effective also in unstructured or partially unstructured environments. A modern vision-based yield estimation approach is a complex system capable to detect, track and map the fruits collecting streams of images. Such a system consists of different functional modules, among which the most relevant is certainly the fruit detection module. Its purpose is to detect and locate the fruits within a single image. In this section, we first provide an overview of the methods used for fruit localization and then we analyze how these methodologies are employed for yield estimation. 2.1. Object detection and counting for agriculture applications Fully supervised CNN architectures for detection and counting have achieved impressive results in a wide variety of datasets and tasks (Zhang et al., 2015, 2017; Khan et al., 2016; Bargoti and Un- derwood, 2017a). chunks.text: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence 109 (2022) 104615 Contents lists available at ScienceDirect Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence journal homepage: www.elsevier.com/locate/engappai A novel vision-based weakly supervised framework for autonomous yield estimation in agricultural applications Enrico Bellocchio ∗, Francesco Crocetti, Gabriele Costante, Mario Luca Fravolini, Paolo Valigi Department of Engineering, University of Perugia, 06125 Perugia, Italy A R T I C L E I N F O Keywords: Autonomous systems Automatic yield estimation Weakly-supervised learning Visual learning A B S T R A C T Autonomous systems have been established as a ground-breaking technology in agriculture, particularly for resource optimization and labor savings.
